entities.name: Married Women's Property Acts
entities.label: Movement
entities.summary: Under English common law (coverture), a married woman had no separate legal existence — her property, earnings, and even her body belonged to her husband. Mississippi (1839) passed the first Married Women's Property Act. England followed in 1870 and 1882. These acts slowly restored women's legal personhood.
